rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~91% 25bp / ~9–12% 50bp (CME FedWatch); ECB Dec ~88%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~32–36%; Hammack backs gradual hikes, Daly sees more hikes likely
rows.read: Federal Reserve officials kept making the case for more rate rises, and a December hike is now close to fully priced, with more expected next year. Europe, Britain and Japan are also expected to hike, but US rates are rising faster, so the gap keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q (fcst +0.7%); US jobless claims 200K (fcst 194K), continuing 1.697M; euro-area Q3 GDP 2nd est. Fri 4:00 AM CT
rows.read: UK growth matched forecasts and US layoffs stayed low, so neither economy shows strain yet. The US still looks firmer than Australia, Canada or New Zealand, which keeps the dollar ahead of those currencies.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US Oct CPI +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%; US PPI Fri 7:30 AM CT fcst +0.4% m/m; Japan Oct wholesale prices +7.1% y/y (fcst 6.5%); Brent ~$96
rows.read: US inflation is running at about twice the Fed's goal, and oil's jump on Thursday adds to that worry. That keeps the Fed hiking and supports the dollar. US producer prices on Friday are the next check.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Nvidia shares down sharply after CEO Jensen Huang resigned; AUD/USD ~0.680 (−0.9%), NZD/USD ~0.554 (−0.5%); USD/CHF ~0.834; gold ~$3,874
rows.read: Nvidia's chief executive quit and renewed US–Iran tension hit the mood, but stocks broadly held up, so there was no rush into safe havens. The Aussie and kiwi took the brunt, while the franc and yen drew no extra support.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$96.0, WTI ~$88.9 late Thu (OilPriceAPI); US crude stocks +4.66M vs −1.11M expected (EIA); gold ~$3,874 (−2.8%)
rows.read: Oil jumped after President Trump said the US doesn't need a deal with Iran, while gold slid on higher US yields. Dearer oil helps the Canadian dollar and hurts energy buyers like Japan and the euro area. Gold's drop takes some support from the Aussie.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; 4-week change NZD −22K, EUR −34K contracts; next report Friday
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, and Thursday's moves went their way. Their large bet on the yen keeps losing money as it weakens. The next weekly report is due Friday.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US 10-year ~5.10%; $25B 30-year auction 5.441%, bid-to-cover 2.36 (six-auction avg 2.44); October federal deficit a record for the month (Hercules)
rows.read: Soft demand at this week's US government bond sales, ending with the 30-year on Thursday, pushed long-term borrowing costs back above 5%. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but buyers asking for more pay to hold US debt is a worry if it keeps up.
